meta.titre: Tone and Attitude: reading a writer's voice and identifying the writer
meta.sous_theme: Tone, attitude and the identity of the writer
tags: A Level English - tone and attitude

source.epreuve_titre: GCE A/L English Language past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A reader's letter in a Cameroonian daily newspaper complains about weeks of power cuts and ends with the words, "What a pleasant surprise to live by candlelight again." Nobody reading it thinks the writer is happy: the words say one thing and the writer means another. Examiners at A Level test exactly this skill in comprehension passages, in questions such as "What is the writer's attitude?" or "The writer of this passage is most likely a ...", and in literature questions on how writers make readers laugh. This course shows you how to read a writer's voice, name it precisely and use the right tone in your own writing.

items: A writer chooses words deliberately to show feelings as well as facts.
Adjectives, adverbs and verbs can be positive, negative or neutral in meaning.
A passage has a topic, a purpose (to inform, persuade, entertain or advise) and an intended reader.

sections.titre: Tone and attitude: clues, vocabulary and method
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Tone, attitude and mood
**Tone** is the voice of the writer, the attitude to the subject and the reader that the words reveal. **Attitude** is the opinion itself (approval, disapproval, indifference). **Mood** is the feeling a passage creates in the reader. A question on tone always asks what the writer feels, never what you feel.

### Where tone hides
| Clue | What to look for |
|---|---|
| Diction | Words with a positive or negative colour: "slim" praises, "skinny" criticises. |
| Punctuation | Exclamation marks, rhetorical questions, quotation marks that cast doubt on a word. |
| Sentence shape | Short blunt sentences suggest anger or finality; long flowing ones suggest reflection. |
| Figures of speech | Exaggeration, understatement, irony, comparison. |
| Contrast | Praise attached to something bad signals irony or sarcasm. |

### A working vocabulary of tone
| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| sarcastic | says the opposite of the truth in order to mock or hurt |
| ironic | the meaning differs from, or contrasts with, the surface statement or the expected result |
| satirical | exposes and ridicules faults of people or society, aiming at change |
| cynical | distrusts people's motives and expects the worst |
| nostalgic | longs wistfully for the past |
| indignant | angry because something seems unfair |
| sympathetic | shows pity and understanding |
| objective, detached | reports facts without personal feeling |
| didactic | aims to teach or give a moral lesson |
| ambivalent | holds mixed or conflicting feelings |
| patronising | talks down to the reader |

### Method for a tone question
1. State the topic of the passage in one sentence.
2. Underline words of judgement, punctuation clues and contrasts.
3. Decide whether the attitude is positive, negative or neutral, then choose the most precise word.
4. Compare the surface meaning with the real meaning.
5. Test every option against the whole passage and reject any option that fits only one sentence.

### Humour in literature
When a question asks how writers present their stories humorously, name the device (exaggeration, irony, understatement, comic character, comic situation, wordplay), point to a precise moment in the text you have studied, and explain the effect: laughter that entertains, or laughter that criticises.

variantes.nom: Who is the writer? ("The writer is most likely a ...")
variantes.quand_utiliser: When an item asks you to identify the writer's job, role or relationship to the reader.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Collect four kinds of evidence: the **vocabulary field** (technical words suggest a specialist), the **purpose** (informing, selling, warning, advising), the **audience** (who is addressed, with what politeness) and the **point of view** (first person experience or outside report). Choose the option that the whole passage supports best. Reject an option only because its topic is mentioned in the text: a passage about fish does not have to be written by a fisherman.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a composition asks you to advise, complain, persuade or address a given person.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Match the tone to the reader and the situation. Advice to a distressed person needs a **warm, respectful, non-judgemental** voice, simple direct sentences and practical steps. A formal letter needs polite, formal vocabulary and no slang. A speech may speak directly to the audience and use rhetorical questions. Keep the same tone from the first line to the last.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says that writers are humorous and asks you to illustrate this with texts you have studied.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use only texts you know well. For each text, write: the device, a specific example from the text, and the effect on the reader. Close each paragraph by saying whether the humour is gentle, mocking or critical of society. Never tell the whole story; select one moment per text.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Read the passage and answer the question.

"Once again the council has promised that the market road will be repaired 'very soon'. Traders have heard these words every dry season for six years, and every rainy season the potholes grow deeper, until a small taxi could vanish into one. One must admire such a faithful tradition of promising."

Which word best describes the writer's tone? A. admiring  B. sarcastic  C. neutral  D. nostalgic

etapes.action: State the topic in one sentence.
etapes.justification: Tone is a feeling about something, so you must know what the feeling is about.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The passage is about a promise to repair a road that is repeated every year and never kept.

etapes.justification: Each clue is a small piece of evidence about the writer's attitude.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Quotation marks around 'very soon' show doubt. The repetition "every dry season for six years" shows frustration. The picture of a taxi vanishing into a pothole is an exaggeration used to mock. "One must admire" is a phrase of praise.

etapes.action: Compare the surface meaning with the real meaning.
etapes.justification: If the praise sits beside a failure, the words do not mean what they say.
etapes.resultat_markdown: On the surface the writer praises the council. In reality the writer is criticising it for a broken promise.

etapes.action: Test each option against the whole passage.
etapes.justification: A correct option must fit all the clues, not one sentence.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A takes the praise literally. C ignores the judgement words. D requires a longing for the past, which is absent. B fits every clue.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The answer is **B, sarcastic**. The writer pretends to admire the council but really mocks it. The passage is also ironic and critical, but "sarcastic" is the most precise word because praise is used to mock a target.

items.erreur_markdown: "The tone is admiring because the writer uses the words 'admire' and 'faithful'."
items.pourquoi_faux: The student read the surface words and ignored the context. Praise words placed next to a failure often signal sarcasm.
items.correction_markdown: Ask what the words are praising. If the thing is clearly bad, the praise is ironic and the tone is sarcastic or critical.

items.erreur_markdown: "The tone is sad because the passage made me feel sad."
items.pourquoi_faux: This describes the mood (the effect on the reader), not the tone (the writer's attitude).
items.correction_markdown: Identify what the writer feels about the subject from the words chosen, for example "the tone is regretful".

items.erreur_markdown: "The tone of the passage is bad." or "The tone is good."
items.pourquoi_faux: These words are too vague to earn credit and do not say what the attitude is.
items.correction_markdown: Use a precise word from your vocabulary: critical, indignant, sympathetic, objective, nostalgic, and support it with a quotation.

items.erreur_markdown: "The passage talks about fish, so the writer is a fisherman."
items.pourquoi_faux: The topic alone does not identify the writer. The writer may be a reporter, a trader or a health officer.
items.correction_markdown: Use vocabulary field, purpose, audience and point of view together, and choose the option best supported by the whole passage.

items.erreur_markdown: In a question on humour, retelling the plot of a story.
items.pourquoi_faux: The question asks how humour is created, not what happens in the story.
items.correction_markdown: Name the device, give one precise moment and explain the effect on the reader.

items.enonce_markdown:
Name the tone of each statement with one precise word chosen from this list: sarcastic, objective, nostalgic, indignant.

(a) "How wonderful that the lights failed again, just as the exam began!"
(b) "The committee met on Tuesday and approved the budget."
(c) "I remember the evenings at my grandmother's house, the fire and the stories, and how I miss them."
(d) "How dare they close the clinic without warning the villagers!"
items.solution_markdown: **(a) sarcastic**: the praise "how wonderful" is attached to a bad event. **(b) objective**: it reports facts without feeling or judgement. **(c) nostalgic**: it longs for the past ("I remember", "how I miss them"). **(d) indignant**: the exclamation and "how dare they" show anger at an unfair act.

items.enonce_markdown:
Read the passage and answer both questions.

"I have taught the same Form One class for thirty years, and still, each September, I feel a nervous thrill when the new faces file in. They think the nervous one is me. Perhaps they are right, but I am also delighted."

(a) The writer is most likely a: A. school inspector  B. long-serving teacher  C. new pupil  D. newspaper reporter
(b) Give one word for the writer's tone and support it with a short quotation.
items.solution_markdown: **(a) B, long-serving teacher.** The writer has taught the same class for thirty years and meets the new pupils each September; an inspector, a new pupil or a reporter would not speak like this. **(b) warm (affectionate) or good-humoured.** Support: "I am also delighted" shows pleasure, and the gentle joke in "They think the nervous one is me" shows a friendly attitude to the pupils. Award credit for a precise word and a matching quotation.

items.enonce_markdown: A Lower Sixth student writes to the school counsellor: "I am afraid I will fail my GCE and disappoint my family." Write the counsellor's reply in about 80 words. Then list three features of your wording that make the tone supportive.
items.solution_markdown:
Model reply: "Dear Chi, thank you for trusting me with your worry. Many students feel afraid before the GCE, and the fear shows that you care about your future. Your feelings are understandable. You cannot control the result today, but you can control your preparation. Make a revision timetable, practise past questions each week and rest properly. If you still feel anxious, come to my office and we will plan together. You are not alone." (The model is between 70 and 90 words.)

**Three features:** (1) warm, respectful address and thanks ("thank you for trusting me"); (2) reassurance that normalises the feeling ("many students feel afraid") without judging; (3) practical, encouraging advice and an offer of help ("we will plan together"). Other valid features: simple direct sentences, no blame, positive closing sentence.

items_markdown: Tone is the writer's attitude shown through words; mood is the feeling created in the reader.
Look for clues in diction, punctuation, sentence shape, figures of speech and contrast.
Praise attached to something bad signals irony or sarcasm: never take such words literally.
Name the tone with a precise word (critical, indignant, nostalgic, objective...) and support it with a short quotation.
To identify the writer, combine vocabulary field, purpose, audience and point of view, and choose the best-supported option.
In your own writing, match the tone to the reader and the situation and keep it steady to the end.
